title: Preposition + -ing
note: adjective + preposition + -ing · verb + preposition + -ing · plain prepositions (without / before / after / instead of / by / despite) + -ing · `to` as a preposition (be used to, look forward to) against `to` as an infinitive marker · 4 strands x 12 · 48 items · built to live 2026-08-07 (cloud run 9)

cards.title: After a preposition, the verb takes -ing
cards.body: This is the whole rule, and it has no exceptions: if a verb follows a preposition, it goes into the -ing form.
cards.body_cz: Celé pravidlo, a bez výjimek: stojí-li sloveso po předložce, má tvar -ing.

rows: without
He left without saying goodbye.
before
Check the price before booking the flight.
instead of
Instead of driving, we took the train.
by
You can save money by cooking at home.
despite / in spite of
Despite arriving late, he got a seat.

cards.title: Adjective + preposition: learn the pair, not the word
cards.title_cz: Přídavné jméno + předložka: učte se dvojici, ne slovo
cards.body: The preposition is not predictable from Czech — it belongs to the adjective and has to be learnt with it.
cards.body_cz: Předložka se z češtiny odvodit nedá — patří k přídavnému jménu a je třeba se ji učit spolu s ním.
points: afraid of · tired of · proud of

cards.title: Verb + preposition: the same problem
cards.body: Same rule, same advice: the preposition is part of the verb.
cards.body_cz: Stejné pravidlo, stejná rada: předložka patří ke slovesu.
points: insist on · depend on · agree on

cards.title: The `to` trap: preposition or infinitive marker?
cards.title_cz: Past na `to`: předložka, nebo značka infinitivu?
cards.body: `to` does two different jobs. After want / need / decide / agree it is an infinitive marker and the base form follows. After be used to / get used to / look forward to it is a preposition, so -ing follows. Test it: if you can put a noun after the `to`, it is a preposition.
cards.body_cz: `to` má dvě různé role. Po want / need / decide / agree je to značka infinitivu a následuje základní tvar. Po be used to / get used to / look forward to je to předložka, takže následuje -ing. Test: dá-li se za `to` dosadit podstatné jméno, je to předložka.
points: I want to go. — infinitive marker, base form
I look forward to going. — preposition, -ing
I am used to the noise. → I am used to working at night.
She used to work at night. = a past habit, base form
